checks.name: Diagnosis identifies the exclusive upper bound and a concrete equality/empty counterexample
Real source context was read through a successful completed tool receipt

output.summary: The public inBounds function has an off-by-one error in its upper-bound check: it accepts index === length as valid, violating the contract that valid integer indices for a nonnegative length are 0 through length-1 and that empty collections have no valid index.

findings.title: inBounds accepts index === length (off-by-one upper bound)
findings.body: src/bounds.ts implements inBounds as `index >= 0 && index <= length`. The `<=` admits an index equal to length, but valid indices are only 0..length-1. This also admits index 0 when length is 0, even though empty collections have no valid index. Concrete counterexamples: inBounds(3, 3) evaluates `3 >= 0 && 3 <= 3` => true (expected false); inBounds(0, 0) evaluates `0 >= 0 && 0 <= 0` => true (expected false).
findings.evidence: Line 2: `return index >= 0 && index <= length;`. Frozen counterexamples: {index:3,length:3} expected false observed true; {index:0,length:0} expected false observed true.
findings.suggestion: Use a strict upper-bound comparison: `return index >= 0 && index < length;`

output.diagnosis: The upper-bound comparison uses <= instead of <, so index === length is treated as in-bounds. For length 3 the only valid indices are 0,1,2 (so 3 must be false), and for length 0 no index is valid (so 0 must be false).
